document_title: Tested at Nenana. Awarded in New York. Next stop unnamed.
post_copy:
In June, controlled fires were set along the Nenana-Totchaket Road, and machines from Nenana's airport had 8 hours to find them alone.

Catherine Cahill's UAF drone center ran the airspace. The task was a fire found and fully out in 10 minutes across 1,000 square kilometers. AURA Foresight met the detection gate. XPRIZE's release is silent on full suppression.

Anduril took first place in the autonomous track as $4.55 million was awarded on September 23rd.

Alaska's 2025 season burned 1.68 million acres by XPRIZE's estimate, nearly seven test areas. Next is a 12 to 15 month Impact Phase. Dryad's 2027 pilot plans name no place.

Aerial views over Nenana show the awards, the test area at true size, a scorecard against the clock and a season in test areas.

Whose ground should host the first fire these machines meet that nobody lit?

#XPRIZEWildfire #Nenana #FireDrones

slides.headline: Tested at Nenana.
labels: GOLD SQUARE = THE 1,000 KM² TEST AREA AT TRUE SIZE, PLACED FOR SCALE

slides.kicker: SEPTEMBER 23RD, NEW YORK CITY FIRE MUSEUM
slides.headline: Anduril first. Dryad second. AURA third.
slides.body: XPRIZE paid $4.55 million across both tracks. The autonomous track was decided in the Alaska finals, and Lockheed Martin's $1 million detection bonus also went to Anduril.
labels: ANDURIL $1.2 MILLION + LOCKHEED MARTIN BONUS $1 MILLION
TRACK TOTAL $2.5 MILLION, OR $3.5 MILLION WITH THE BONUS

slides.headline: The exam was flown from Nenana's airport
slides.body: For two weeks in June the finalists flew from Nenana Municipal Airport. UAF's drone center, ACUASI, managed the airspace. The test site lay along the Nenana-Totchaket Road corridor.

slides.kicker: THE TASK, AS XPRIZE SET IT
slides.headline: One fire. Ten minutes. 1,000 square kilometers.
slides.body: Each team's machines watched alone for 8 hours. The goal was to detect and fully suppress a high-risk fire within 10 minutes of ignition.
labels: TRUE SIZE, CENTERED ON THE AIRPORT FOR SCALE. NO SOURCE GIVES THE BOUNDARY.

slides.headline: One 10 minute gate is on the record, for detection
slides.body: XPRIZE says AURA met the 10 minute detection gate. Dryad says it detected and verified the fire in 12 minutes or less. XPRIZE's release doesn't say any team fully suppressed a fire inside 10 minutes.
labels: THE GOAL, DETECT AND SUPPRESS, PER XPRIZE
DRYAD, DETECT AND VERIFY, PER DRYAD
SUPPRESSION IN 10, NOT IN XPRIZE'S RELEASE

slides.headline: "The final prize remains on the horizon"
Alaska's 2025 fires covered nearly seven test areas
slides.body: XPRIZE estimates Alaska's 2025 season burned 1.68 million acres. That is about 6,800 square kilometers, the 1,000 km² test area nearly seven times over. The tiles show area only, not where anything burned.
labels: AREA ONLY, NOT WHERE IT BURNED

slides.headline: What comes next names no Alaska address
slides.body: XPRIZE now moves to a 12 to 15 month Impact Phase to turn these systems into deployable tools. Dryad plans pilots in 2027 and names no location. The only Alaska institutions in the record are UAF and ACUASI.

slides.headline: Alaska hosted the exam. Should it get a seat in the Impact Phase?

aftercare: Post today, Thursday September 24th, between 8 and 11am AKT, while the September 23rd awards are a day old. If the draft is read after 11am, hold it for Tuesday September 29th, 8 to 11am AKT. When to post is your call.
Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting, as plain text, so every raw URL stays a live link.

Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. If someone asks whether any team met the full 10 minute suppression goal, the answer is that XPRIZE's release doesn't say, and Lockheed Martin's Adam Broecker said the final prize remains on the horizon. Never say the prize went unclaimed, because no source says that.

Story note. XPRIZE and Dryad are the only sources, and no Alaska newsroom had covered the awards when this was drafted, so a correction from someone at Nenana, UAF or state fire staff is worth pinning. If a reader asks about other Interior decisions, the Eielson microreactor site comment window closes September 30th (the docket item, from KUAC's September 20th report).
After 48 hours, note saves and comments, and whether any Alaska outlet has picked up the awards since.
